<tr><td>

On Windows, Flisk runs inside **Ubuntu on WSL2**. [WSL2](../start/words.md#wsl2) is a free part of Windows that runs Linux, and **Ubuntu** is the Linux app it installs. You set it up once; after that, you type every Flisk command in the Ubuntu app. Every grey box below is a [command](../start/words.md#command): copy it, paste it and press Enter. Never written code? [Start here](../start/first-time.md).

**For developers:** native Windows runs only inspection commands (`flisk --version`, `flisk doctor`, `flisk up --dry-run`); `flisk up` there refuses and points to WSL2.

**1. Install Ubuntu on WSL2.** Open the Start menu, type `PowerShell`, right-click **Windows PowerShell** and choose **Run as administrator**. In PowerShell, paste this and press Enter:

```powershell
wsl --install -d Ubuntu
```

Restart your computer if Windows asks you to. Then open the **Ubuntu** app from the Start menu: it is your [terminal](../start/words.md#terminal) from now on. The first time, it asks you to choose a user name and password for Ubuntu.

**2. Only for bigger apps: Docker.** You need it when your app has a [database](../start/words.md#database), one web address in front of all its parts (a gateway URL), or must run in the same [container](../start/words.md#container) you deploy. Then install [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) with the WSL 2 backend. In Docker Desktop, open **Settings → Resources → WSL Integration**, turn it on for Ubuntu, and click **Apply & Restart**. This lets the Ubuntu app use [Docker](../start/words.md#docker).

**3. In the Ubuntu terminal**, install Tilt and Flisk, then check your computer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tilt-dev/tilt/master/scripts/install.sh \
  | bash
curl -fsSL https://flisk.sh/install.sh | sh
flisk doctor
```

The first command installs [Tilt](../start/words.md#tilt), the second installs Flisk, and [`flisk doctor`](../start/words.md#flisk-doctor) checks your computer and prints a fix for anything missing. To check that Flisk itself is installed, run `flisk --version`: it prints a version number.

Run every Flisk command from Ubuntu, not from PowerShell. The [Windows & WSL2 guide](../wsl2.md) has the full walkthrough, an example stack to try, and troubleshooting.
